sources.quote: Major US Banks Use TCS, Other Middlemen To Hire Lower Paid H-1B Visa Workers
sources.searcher_note: Headline only; WebFetch got HTTP 403. Bloomberg's Facebook post and syndications date it about 2025-06-27. Compares contractor pay with the client's own H-1B hires (Citigroup, Capital One), the same comparison as the lead.

sources.quote: Median salary for one of these H-1B developers? $94,000. Compare that to $142,000 for a direct hire doing similar work.
sources.searcher_note: Retells Bloomberg's Citigroup numbers: contractor H-1B developers $94K median vs $142K for direct hires, May 2020-May 2024. Same measure as the lead, other window, one named client. Whether Citi is among the lead's 45 is unknown.

sources.quote: But top outsourcing firms paid well below this number, with TCS paying as little as $72,000 on average.
sources.searcher_note: Early pattern coverage: outsourcers pay H-1Bs less than Apple, Cisco, Microsoft and Google (over $120K). Credits part of the gap to degree mix: direct employers hire more Master's holders.

sources.quote: Their business model relies on flooding the lottery with registrations for mid-career staff in routine roles, who often qualify for higher wage levels despite the relatively low actual pay.
sources.searcher_note: Possible tension with the lead's caveat: IFP says outsourcers' workers often get HIGHER DOL wage levels despite low pay. The lead says most of the gap is the lower skill level contractors write down.

notes: Pattern coverage is strong and old. EPI (Costa and Hira, 'H-1B visas and prevailing wage levels', uses FY2019 LCA data) and EPI's 'outsourcing visa' blog were found, but WebFetch and curl got HTTP 403, so no quotes were taken. Bloomberg's 2024 piece 'Thousands of H-1B Visas Are Going to Middlemen Gaming the System' (https://www.bloomberg.com/graphics/2024-staffing-firms-game-h1b-visa-lottery-system/) also returned 403. A search summary tied it to 'a typical contractor was paid about $48,000 less than a worker employed directly by the company that sponsored her visa' and top-10 medians of $120K in-house vs $72K contractor. Neither sentence was verified on a live page, so neither is recorded. No source found gives the lead's specific test: contractor LCA wages vs the client's own LCA wages, same SOC code and state, 45 clients, FY2019, median 20.6% (6.6% at the same wage level, 14.5% for new hires). The Durbin-Grassley press release of 2025-09-25 (https://www.durbin.senate.gov/newsroom/press-releases/durbin-grassley-take-aim-at-labor-exploitation-in-tech-finance-retail-sectors) sent letters to TCS, Cognizant, Deloitte and big tech clients but gives no contractor-vs-client wage figure. Recent coverage (Sept 2026) is about the $100K H-1B fee and a Trump order investigating H-1B hiring, not this wage gap. 7 searches were run.
